label: S. 4938

latest_action.text: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Bycatch Reduction Act aims to reduce the impacts of trawl fishing gear on bycatch and seafloor habitats in the Bering Sea, Aleutian Islands, and Gulf of Alaska. The bill sets up gear performance standards, requires seafloor contact detection and salmon excluder devices, improves transparency and public participation in the North Pacific Fishery Management Council, prioritizes ecosystem and salmon life history research, modernizes electronic monitoring, prohibits certain unsustainable foreign seafood imports, and establishes financial assistance funds for cleaner fishing gear.

affected_groups.effect: Must meet new gear performance standards, install seafloor contact detection systems and salmon excluder devices, and comply with enhanced electronic monitoring and data submission rules.
affected_groups.group: Commercial fishing vessel owners and operators using trawl gear in the Bering Sea, Aleutian Islands, and Gulf of Alaska

affected_groups.effect: Subject to stricter transparency rules, mandatory recorded roll call votes, updated public comment periods, and new requirements to establish gear baselines and performance standards.
Prohibited from importing seafood into the United States unless the originating fishery meets conservation standards comparable to U.S. laws, subject to cargo seizure upon violation.
affected_groups.group: Seafood importers and foreign vessel owners

affected_groups.effect: Involved in consultations and public-private research partnerships regarding salmon life history, ecosystem analyses, and bycatch mitigation.
affected_groups.group: Subsistence, commercial, and recreational fishing participants and Alaska Native communities

key_provisions: Establishes a pelagic trawl gear performance standard and requires applicable vessels to use seafloor contact detection systems to monitor net positions relative to the seafloor.
Requires nonpelagic trawl catcher/processor vessels to use modified footropes and trawl sweeps to reduce seafloor contact within specified timelines.
Mandates that all vessels using pelagic trawl gear in specified North Pacific fisheries be equipped with operational salmon excluder devices.
Improves public transparency for the North Pacific Fishery Management Council by requiring recorded roll call votes, live webcasts, searchable transcripts, and a permanent online archive.
Prohibits importing seafood from foreign vessels or owners unless the Secretary of Commerce determines the fishery harvests fish comparably to U.S. conservation standards.
Authorizes $10,000,000 annually from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for the NOAA Bycatch Reduction Engineering Program and establishes a Bycatch Mitigation and Habitat Protection Assistance Fund.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts or specific appropriations for most programs outside of the $10,000,000 annual authorization for the Bycatch Reduction Engineering Program.
Precise details on civil penalty amounts or specific permit sanction structures beyond referencing existing Magnuson-Stevens Act enforcement mechanisms.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Bycatch Reduction Act aims to reduce the impacts of trawl fishing gear on bycatch and seafloor habitats in the Bering Sea, Aleutian Islands, and Gulf of Alaska. The bill sets up gear performance standards, requires seafloor contact detection and salmon excluder devices, improves transparency and public participation in the North Pacific Fishery Management Council, prioritizes ecosystem and salmon life history research, modernizes electronic monitoring, prohibits certain unsustainable foreign seafood imports, and establishes financial assistance funds for cleaner fishing gear.
summary_detail.significance: The bill introduces sweeping regulatory changes to North Pacific trawl fisheries intended to protect marine benthic habitats and reduce the incidental catch of species such as salmon and crab. It substantially increases federal oversight, data collection requirements, and public transparency for regional fisheries management, while altering foreign seafood import rules based on U.S.-comparable conservation standards.
